claim: Let T be an S_4 tournament on 52 vertices and assume (input, research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md) that every tight pair has J >= 6. (A) No vertex has in-degree 23; hence every in-degree is >= 24, Z = {d^- = 24} has |Z| <= 5 and sum_x max(e(x),0) = 26 + |Z|. The proof is a trace/Frobenius rank inequality on the tight block of the Gram matrix of Corollary 3, not Gershgorin; its threshold is exactly J_min = 6 (J_min = 5 does not suffice; J_min = 7 would already close the case by counting alone). (B) For a vertex v of in-degree 24 the Gershgorin step of Corollary 3 holds at a tight row iff J >= 9 (row sum 14 - J vs diagonal 6; J = 8 is the equality case), and in the best case (no tight row of v with J <= 8) it gives only E_A <= 12 and W_A <= 14, while the J >= 6 lower bound gives W_A >= 6. In general t <= 24 + d + b, hence E_A <= 12 + d + b, where d = number of tight sets shared by two tight rows (possible only for J <= 8) and b = number of distinct tight sets with J in {6,7,8}, no cover vertex, and in-block heavy weight >= 6 (pair-level CP-SAT says b counts only J in {7,8}). (C) In-degree 24 is NOT excluded: even a perfect spectral step leaves the window 6 <= W_A <= 14 open, so the bottleneck at N = 52 is a lower bound on E_A, not the eigenvalue step. Combining with the global budget gives no contradiction. Erdos 902 is not solved.
definitions: For a vertex v: A = N^-(v), B = N^+(v), r = |A| = d^-(v). Rows are z in V \ {v} (51 rows). D_z = D({v,z}) = A cap N^-(z), h_z = |D_z| - 11 >= 0 (F2). Row z is tight if h_z = 0. t = number of tight rows, t_A, t_B those with z in A, z in B. E_A = sum_{x in A} e(x), W_A = sum_{x in A} max(e(x),0).
G = Gram matrix of the indicator vectors 1_{D_z} in R^A (51 x 51, rank <= r). M = G - 5*11^T: M_zz = 6 + h_z, M_zz' = |D({v,z,z'})| - 5 >= 0 (F1).

For a tight row z: R_z = D_z, O_z = V \ ({v,z} cup R_z) (39 vertices), q_y(z) = |R_z cap N^-(y)|, e_y(z) = q_y(z) - 5, J(z) = sum_{r in R_z} e(r) (>= 6 by the input; e >= 0 on R_z by Lemma T). A cover of z is y in O_z with Q_y = R_z (e_y = 6).
sigma(J) = max sum of squares of reals x_i in [0,6] with sum x_i <= 14 - J = 36*floor((14-J)/6) + ((14-J) mod 6)^2: sigma(5)=45, sigma(6)=40, sigma(7)=37, sigma(8)=36, sigma(9)=25.
U = a set of representatives of the distinct tight sets D_z; d = number of tight sets carried by two tight rows; heavy weight of z inside a row set S: w_S(z) = sum_{z' in S, z' != z} M_zz'.
argument: LEMMA 1 (tight rows). For a tight row z: M_zz' = 0 for z' in R_z, M_zz' = e_{z'}(z) in [0,6] for z' in O_z, the off-diagonal row sum is 14 - J(z), and the off-diagonal square sum is <= sigma(J(z)). Proof: by (2.1) of the hand proof, D({v,z,z'}) = R_z cap N^-(z'); for z' in R_z this is the in-degree 5 of z' in the 5-regular T[R_z]. Each r in R_z has d^+(r) = 26 - e(r) and beats v, z and 5 vertices of R_z, so it beats 19 - e(r) vertices of O_z; summing, sum_y q_y = 209 - J and sum_{y in O_z} e_y = 209 - J - 5*39 = 14 - J. The square sum is a convex function on the polytope {0 <= x_i <= 6, sum x_i <= 14 - J}, maximised at a vertex (all coordinates 0 or 6 except one), giving sigma(J). QED

LEMMA 2 (rank). Every principal submatrix M_S has at most r positive eigenvalues, and if tr M_S >= 0 then (tr M_S)^2 <= r * ||M_S||_F^2. Proof: G is PSD of rank <= r, so lambda_{r+1}(G) = 0; M = G - 5*11^T with 5*11^T PSD, so lambda_i(M) <= lambda_i(G) (Weyl) and lambda_{r+1}(M) <= 0; Cauchy interlacing gives lambda_{r+1}(M_S) <= lambda_{r+1}(M) <= 0. With p <= r positive eigenvalues, tr M_S <= sum_{lambda>0} lambda <= sqrt(p * sum_{lambda>0} lambda^2) <= sqrt(r ||M_S||_F^2). QED. (If every row of S is tight, X_S 1_A = 11*1, so M_S = X_S (I - (5/121) J_r) X_S^T is even PSD for r <= 24; not needed.)

THEOREM A (Corollary 2 at N = 52: in-degree 23 is impossible). Suppose d^-(v) = 23, so |A| = 23, |B| = 28. (a) In T[A] every in-degree |D({a,v})| is >= 11 (F3) and they sum to C(23,2) = 23*11, so T[A] is 11-regular, every A-row is tight and D_a = A cap N^-(a). (b) Every a' in A beats some a in A, so a' in D({a,v}) and e(a') >= 0 (Lemma T). (c) sum_{a in A} J(a) = sum_{r in A} e(r) |N^+(r) cap A| = 11 E_A, and each J(a) >= 6, so 11 E_A >= 138, E_A >= 13. (d) Arcs A -> B: a beats v and 11 vertices of A, so 14 - e(a) vertices of B; hence sum_{b in B} |D_b| = 322 - E_A and sum_{b in B} h_b = 322 - E_A - 11*28 = 14 - E_A. So E_A in {13, 14} and at most one B-row is non-tight: t >= 50. (e) Let S be the tight rows. M_S has diagonal 6 (tr = 6t) and, by Lemma 1 with J >= 6, ||M_S||_F^2 <= t(36 + 40) = 76t. Lemma 2 with r = 23: 36 t^2 <= 23 * 76 t, i.e. t <= 48.56, contradicting t >= 50. QED. Threshold: with J >= 5 only, (c)-(d) give t >= 48 and (e) gives t <= 51.75 (no contradiction); with J >= 7, (c) gives E_A >= 161/11 > 14, contradicting (d) without any spectral step. So J_min = 6 is exactly where the Frobenius step is needed and where it suffices.

COROLLARY. Under the input, every in-degree at N = 52 is >= 24, so e(x) >= -1, Z = {e = -1}, |Z| <= 5 (Claim Q), at most 2 in-neighbours of a Z-vertex lie in Z, and sum_x max(e(x),0) = 26 + |Z| <= 31.

PROPOSITION B (Corollary 3 bookkeeping, d^-(v) = 24). |A| = 24, |B| = 27. In T[A] in-degrees sum to C(24,2) = 276 = 24*11 + 12, so sum_{z in A} h_z = 12 and t_A >= 12. Arcs A -> B: x in A beats 26 - e(x) - 1 - (12 - h_x) vertices of B, so sum_{z in B} |D_z| = 324 - E_A and sum_{z in B} h_z = 27 - E_A; hence E_A <= 27, t_B >= E_A and t >= 12 + E_A. Also E_A >= W_A - 2 (Claim Q) and W_A >= 6: the >= 12 tight A-rows have J(a) = sum_{x in D_a} e(x) >= 6 with e >= 0 on D_a, and sum_{a} J(a) <= sum_{x in A} max(e(x),0) |N^+(x) cap A| <= 12 W_A, so 72 <= 12 W_A. (If all tight A-rows had J >= 9 the same count gives W_A >= 9.)

PROPOSITION C (exact Gershgorin threshold). By Lemma 1 a tight row has diagonal 6 and off-diagonal sum 14 - J: strictly dominant iff J >= 9, equal at J = 8, and 7 or 8 > 6 at J = 7, 6. Hence any set K of tight rows with w_K(z) <= 5 for all z in K (in particular K = tight rows with J >= 9) has M_K positive definite, and by Lemma 2 |K| <= 24. Rows with J >= 8: M_K = 6I + N with N >= 0 of row sums <= 6, so M_K is PSD and is singular only on a connected component C of the heavy graph on which every row has J = 8, all of its heavy weight inside C, and C bipartite (Perron-Frobenius: -rho(N_C) = -6 is an eigenvalue of an irreducible nonnegative N_C iff N_C is bipartite with rho = 6, and rho = 6 with row sums <= 6 forces all row sums = 6). Consequence: t <= 24 + t_{<=8} (t_{<=8} = tight rows with J <= 8), so E_A <= 12 + t_{<=8} and W_A <= 14 + t_{<=8}. Best case t_{<=8} = 0: E_A <= 12, W_A <= 14. Compare N = 51 (W <= 2 < 3 <= J): at N = 52 the analogue J({a,v}) <= W_A <= 14 is compatible with J in [9,14], so the step gives no contradiction even in the best case.

PROPOSITION D (strengthening for J in {6,7,8}). D1 (duplicates): if tight rows z != z' have D_z = D_z' = R then J(z) = J(z') <= 8, no third tight row has the set R, and z, z' are not both in A. Proof: z' is not in D_{z'} = R and z' != v, z, so z' in O_z with q_{z'}(z) = |R cap N^-(z')| = 11, e = 6 <= 14 - J; a third such row would give 12 <= 14 - J, J <= 2, contradicting J >= 6. If z, z' in A with z -> z', then z in A cap N^-(z') = R = A cap N^-(z), absurd. D2 (distinct sets): replace the tight rows by U (one row per distinct set). M_U is a principal submatrix, so it has <= 24 positive eigenvalues. If z has a cover y, then y is either non-tight (not in U) or tight with D_y superset of R_z of size 11, i.e. D_y = R_z (same set, not a second element of U); so w_U(z) <= 14 - J(z) - 6 * #covers. Hence Gershgorin holds strictly at row z of U whenever J(z) >= 9 or z has a cover (then w_U(z) <= 2). D3: let b = #{z in U : J(z) in {6,7,8}, no cover, w_U(z) >= 6}. U minus these rows is strictly dominant inside itself, so |U| - b <= 24 and t = |U| + d <= 24 + d + b, giving E_A <= 12 + d + b. A bad row with J = 8 has all of its heavy weight 6 on tight rows of distinct sets (entries <= 5); with J = 7 at most one unit of heavy weight lies outside U. D4 (pair level, solver output): every J = 6 survivor of the pair-level system needs a cover, so b counts only J in {7,8}; J = 7 and J = 8 no-cover survivors exist (patterns 5+2, 5+1+1, 4+2, 3+3, 5+1, 4+1+1). D5 (limit of weighted Gershgorin): for symmetric N >= 0 a positive scaling w with N w < 6 w exists iff rho(N) < 6 (Collatz-Wielandt), so weighted Gershgorin certifies exactly rho(N_U) < 6; anything stronger must use the bipartite/sign structure of N. D6 (second moment): Lemma 2 on all tight rows gives t <= 24(36 + 40)/36 < 51, and on U with entries <= 5 gives |U| <= 24(36 + 34)/36 < 47; both are far above t >= 12 + E_A, so second moments cannot help at in-degree 24 (they work at in-degree 23 only because there t >= 50).

PROPOSITION E (global budget). (i) delta^- >= 24, |Z| <= 5, sum max(e,0) = 26 + |Z| <= 31. (ii) Each v in Z is the head of >= 12 tight pairs {a,v}, a -> v (these are distinct for distinct heads), so T has >= 12|Z| tight pairs; v has >= 12 + E_A(v) tight rows, 6 <= W_A(v) <= 29, and E_A(v) <= 12 + d(v) + b(v). (iii) Every tight pair P has D(P) cap Z = empty and J(P) in [6,14]: its 11 dominators carry >= 6 of the <= 31 units of positive excess. (iv) If Z is empty, every in-degree is 25 + e with e >= 0, sum e = 26, so >= 26 vertices have in-degree 25; a vertex of in-degree d is the head of >= d - d(d-23)/2 tight pairs, which is <= 0 for d >= 25, so no tight pair is forced. (v) No contradiction follows: with in-degree 24 present, the local constraints are consistent with E_A in [4, 12] even under a perfect spectral step; with Z empty, the tight-pair branch is not forced at all and the no-tight branch is untouched.
evidence: research/compute/r8d_thresholds.py (exact arithmetic, no solver): sigma(J) by formula and brute force for J = 3..14; Gershgorin strict iff J >= 9; Corollary 2 at N = 52: Jmin = 5 gives t >= 48 vs Frobenius t <= 51.75 (no contradiction), Jmin = 6 gives t >= 50 vs t <= 48.556 (contradiction), Jmin >= 7 contradicts already by counting; Corollary 3: Frobenius t <= 50.667 (needs E_A >= 39), distinct-set version u <= 46.667.

J = 6, partitions (2,2,1,1), (2,1,1,1,1), (1^6): INFEASIBLE, i.e. a cover is forced at pair level. All 6 J = 7 and all 9 J = 8 surviving partitions remain feasible without a cover.

research/compute/r8d_frobenius_sanity.py (numpy, 400 random instances, 0 violations): <= r positive eigenvalues of X X^T - 5 J, the trace/Frobenius inequality on random principal submatrices, PSD of M when all rows have weight 11 and r <= 24, invariance of the positive-eigenvalue count under duplicated rows. A random 51 x 23 family has mean off-diagonal row square sum about 81, so the bound 40 of Lemma 1 is a genuine structural restriction.
All statements in 'argument' except D4 are proved by hand above; D4 is solver output.
weaknesses: Everything is conditional on the input 'every tight pair at N = 52 has J >= 6'. J = 5 is hand-proved in research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md, but J <= 4 rests on the R1-C and R3-C reports, and the pair-level reproduction of J <= 5 is CP-SAT output without certificate.

Theorem A only uses J >= 6 for the tight pairs {v,z} through the in-degree-23 vertex; besides that it uses only (F1)-(F3) and Lemma T (Claim Q is not needed). It has not been independently reviewed (status proved-unreviewed in the sense of the brief).
In-degree 24 is not excluded. The quantities d (shared tight sets) and b (bad J in {7,8} rows) are not bounded, and even with d = b = 0 the conclusion E_A <= 12 does not contradict anything.
D4 (J = 6 forces a cover) is pair-level solver output, not a hand proof; it only sharpens the definition of b and is not used in Theorem A.
The global statement (E) is bookkeeping; it does not touch the no-tight branch.

next_step: In-degree 24 at N = 52 needs a lower bound E_A(v) >= 13 + d + b for a vertex v of in-degree 24, i.e. it must come from the combinatorics of the tight rows, not from the eigenvalue step. Concretely: (1) bound d by showing two tight pairs {v,z}, {v,z'} cannot share a dominator set (a cover y = z' of a J <= 8 tight pair); the pair {z,z'} then has D({z,z'}) superset of R, which may be attackable with the pair-level rows of {v,z}; (2) for v in Z, combine t_B >= E_A with J(z) >= 6 on the B-rows and the out-degree bound |N^+(x) cap B| = 13 - e(x) + h_x to push E_A up, or show directly that E_A <= 12 is incompatible with the 12 tight A-rows (each with J >= 6 drawn from W_A <= 14 units); (3) hand-prove D4 (J = 6 forces a cover) to make the J = 6 rows unconditional in the spectral bound. If in-degree 24 falls, T has all in-degrees in {25, 26, ...} with sum e = 26 and the remaining work is the tight/no-tight analysis of a near-regular tournament.
relation_to_prior: R3-F located the first failing bound of Corollary 2 at order 52; research/N52_TIGHT_J_GE_6.md noted that Corollary 3's Gershgorin step needs J >= 9. This report (i) closes Corollary 2 at N = 52 under J >= 6 by replacing Gershgorin with a trace/Frobenius rank bound on the tight block, (ii) gives the exact thresholds (Gershgorin: J >= 9, equality at 8; Frobenius at in-degree 23: J >= 6), (iii) shows that at in-degree 24 no strengthening of the spectral step alone can suffice, since the order-51 finish (W <= 2 < 3 <= J) becomes W_A <= 14 vs J >= 6 at order 52, and (iv) gives the duplicate/cover refinement t <= 24 + d + b. It does not repeat any exhausted approach key.
novelty: New: the in-degree-23 exclusion at N = 52 (conditional on J >= 6), via the bound (tr M_S)^2 <= r ||M_S||_F^2 together with the exact square-sum cap sigma(6) = 40 of a tight row; the duplicate-set lemma (a tight dominator set is shared by at most two rows through v, only when J <= 8); the cover reduction of the Gershgorin step on distinct tight sets; the pair-level fact that J = 6 forces a cover (solver); and the observation that at N = 52 the obstruction to excluding in-degree 24 is the lower bound on E_A, not the spectral bound.
